newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 4.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BERLIN - Top German television groups ProSieben Media AG and the RTL network say they will raise advertising prices for their stations in 1998. In their annual ad price announcements, the groups' media marketing agencies Media Gruppe Muenchen and IP Deutschland say market conditions had created conditions for higher asking prices for television ads. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Public television broadcaster ARD says it has succeeded in unseating previous number one station RTL in the July ratings race. With a 15 percent viewer share during the month, ARD edged past RTL, which posted a 14.8 percent share. ARD cited figures provided by the GfK market research institute. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Volkswagen AG, the largest carmaker in Europe, finally joins the big leagues of sports sponsorship when its hometown team of Wolfsburg plays its first match in Germany's first-division Bundesliga. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The Duesseldorf office of the McCann media agency, Universalcommunication Media Intensiv, is being closed due to reorganisation of the agency. McCann plans to concentrate its business in Frankfurt and Nuremberg. (Horizont)

VIENNA - Fast-food chain McDonalds Austria is in a pickle over its latest advertising gimmick, which has placemats featuring a map of the country as devised by Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler. McDonalds told Die Kurier daily that it had simply wanted to highlight the beef-producing regions of Austria on the paper mats which cover its trays. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

HAMBURG - European Union Commissioner Karel van Miert plans to review a German digital television alliance to see if it poses a threat to competition, the newsweekly Der Spiegel says. The "critical point" for van Miert is the participation of Deutsche Telekom AG in an alliance with media giants Bertelsmann and the Kirch Group, the magazine says. (Reuter)

WALLDORF - German software group SAP AG and computer chip maker Intel Corp plan to announce an Internet commerce joint venture on August 5, SAP says. SAP said the goal of the venture was to develop a software product that supports business applications on the Internet. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Media giant Bertelsmann and publishing company Axel-Springer-Verlag launch an Internet sport channel, Sport 1. The online channel offers 24-hour sports news and scores at no cost. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Television production firm Brainpool and station ProSieben start a programming partnership. (Kress)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - Industrial production rises by 1.4 percent in June from May after output figures for the previous month were revised sharply downwards to show a 1.5 percent fall, the Economics Ministry says. The ministry said that the data, which were preliminary, were likely to be revised up substantially. (Reuter)

BONN - Daimler-Benz AG management board member Eckhard Cordes will pay a fine for revealing a rough estimate of 1996 financial results, but maintains he did not break securities trading regulations, Daimler says. Stuttgart prosecutors had been investigating Cordes for allegedly breaking German insider trading laws when in March he provided a small group of journalists with a prediction of 1996 profit figures which had not yet been made public. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Germany's manufacturing sector grew at a slower pace in July according to a BME/Reuters survey, which analysts say indicates the Bundesbank will refrain from an interest rate rise unless the mark keeps weakening. (Reuter)

BONN - The European Commission is to continue to demand repayment of all state subsidies paid to German car-maker Volkswagen that contravene a Commission ruling on the matter, a newspaper says. German business daily Handelsblatt quoted European Commission competition official Alexander Schaub as saying the EC would demand repayment all grants blocked by it in a June 1996 ruling. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Peter Lewandowski becomes editor-in-chief of German Playboy, effective January 1. Lewandowski is currently copy editor and member of the editorial board of women's magazine Marie Claire. (Horizont)
